newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mostly up, pork bellies mostly off.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mostly up, pork bellies mostly off.

text.p: CME hog futures eased late but closed mostly higher while pork belly futures fell to mostly lower closes on technical sell stops, traders said.

Hog futures closed 0.100 cent per lb lower to 0.425 higher with February off 0.025 at 77.625 cents. Lightly traded deferred contracts were up most. Pork bellies finished 0.950 lower to 0.050 higher with February off most at 78.575 cents.

Hog futures trade was light with prices holding in a narrow range on mixed fundamentals, floor sources said. Higher cash hog prices due to adverse weather was supportive but weaker cash pork prices and technicals pressured nearbys, traders said.

Snow and bitter cold temperatures are hampering movement of hogs and in turn, the ability of packers to slaughter hogs. But cash markets could be under pressure next week if temperatures moderate and allow increased movement, they said.

However, underlying support in nearby contracts and continued strength in deferreds will continued to reflect the recent bullish Hogs and Pigs report which showed a much lighter than expected pig crop, they added.
"No one expects markets to stay weak for long. We did have a bullish pig crop report," a trader said of recent USDA data.

Lind-Waldock sold February on the break from early highs with Cargill Investor Services a seller late. Demand was mixed. In hog options, volatility was weak in February on scattered offering of February 78 straddle. LFG bought July 72 puts, pit sources said.

Pork bellies showed early short covering support but slipped in technical buy stops late on scattered selling interest. February held a major trend line early but pressure from steady to weak cash prices pushed prices down into the technical selloff, traders said.

The cash belly market is usually strong during January and product moves out of storage at times, but prices have been drifting lower and storings were larger than expected. High prices may have cut off retail demand, they said.
Rand Financials lightly sold late after early buying by R.J. O'Brien and locals. E.D.&F. Man sold in early dealings, pit sources said.
